### Observed differences

- Two segments swapped their order. In the earlier window, A21 preceded A30, A31 and A36 in all 200 traces, and A22 likewise preceded all three in all 200 traces; in the later window, A30, A31 and A36 each precede A21 and each precede A22 in about 199 of 200 traces, while all these activities still occur together in every trace. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Relative positions shifted accordingly: in the later window the mean position of A30, A31 and A36 each dropped from about 0.59 to about 0.41 of the trace, while A21 rose from about 0.53 to 0.62 and A22 from about 0.38 to 0.47. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Successors changed: in the earlier window A20 led only to A22, whereas in the later window it leads to A30, A31 or A36 in roughly equal thirds (about 33 in 100 observed transitions each). A21 previously led into the group (A36 about 38 in 100, A30 about 34, A31 about 28) and now leads almost exclusively to A25 (about 995 in 1000). Each of A30, A31 and A36 previously led to A25 in about 29–37 of 100 transitions; in the later window each leads to A22 in about 31–34 of 100 and practically never to A25. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Step distances match: A20–A22 was adjacent in all 200 earlier traces and is about 4 steps apart in about 199 of 200 later traces; A21–A25 went from 4 steps apart to adjacent. The ordered pairs from A21 into each group activity and from each group activity into A25, previously seen within five steps in all 200 traces, are now seen within five steps in essentially no trace (each of these six items rests on a single later-window observation). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a placement change: the block A30–A31–A36, executed in varying internal order, and the segment containing A22 and A21 exchanged their relative order, and A25 changed its attachment. In the earlier window the flow ran A20 → A22 → … → A21 → {A30/A31/A36} → A25; in the later window it runs A20 → {A30/A31/A36} → A22 → … → A21 → A25, with A25 now immediately following A21 instead of closing the group. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Supporting signs: the order reversal is shown directly by six activity-pair relations that flip from 100% one way to about 995 in 1000 the other way, and it is consistently corroborated by the successor changes, the step-distance changes and the position shifts; every involved activity occurs in essentially all traces in both windows, so this is not a participation or path-frequency change; and 24 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.41 expected by chance, far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Limitations: the relation between A22 and A21 itself is not observed and A22 has no outgoing profile in the evidence, so the wiring of the middle segment is inferred from positions; six LAG items rest on a single later-window observation each, though the relations they reflect are independently shown by REL and DIR. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is two independent reroutings (A20 into the group, the group into A22, and A21 into A25) rather than one block relocation, since both would produce the same observable order. [LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
